headline: University of West Florida orders dorms evacuated on less than a day’s notice
summary: Hurricane Isaias prompts University of West Florida to create an emergency shelter for students, drawing criticism from some parents for lack of earlier communication.

headline: MVSU basketball player was reportedly warned about his expired immigration status years before ICE detained him
summary: The Mississippi Valley State University basketball player from China, Qingfang Pang, had been warned twice about his expired visa before his arrest by ICE. Monroe University advised him in 2024, and MVSU did so recently before his detention. Pang's attorney was unaware of the previous warning from Monroe. Pang is currently in ICE custody.

headline: Standing Rock Sioux Tribe files lawsuit to shut down Dakota Access Pipeline
summary: The Standing Rock Sioux Tribe has again filed a lawsuit challenging the Dakota Access Pipeline, citing threats to their water supply and treaty rights, reigniting decade-long protests against the pipeline.

headline: Officials take another look at hospital use of offshore captive insurance companies
summary: Maryland officials are investigating whether nonprofit hospitals are evading state taxes by storing billions in captive insurance companies in the Cayman Islands. A whistleblower estimates up to $3 billion could be owed to the state. Hospitals claim they're not gaining tax advantages, but a study is underway to determine if changes in policy are needed.

headline: Chester County high school closes after measles exposure
summary: Measles outbreak at Oxford Area High School in Chester County prompts temporary closure, impacting over 1,200 students; health officials advise unvaccinated individuals to stay away for 21 days; Pennsylvania has seen 1,136 measles cases this year, with 12 counties experiencing community transmission.

headline: School budgets run on diesel
summary: Rising diesel prices are straining Vermont's K-12 school budgets, limiting funds available for other educational expenses and potentially impacting services for vulnerable students.

headline: A rural Oklahoma hospital is bringing back maternity care. Can it survive healthcare cuts?
summary: Oklahoma's Newman Memorial Hospital plans to restore maternity care, with a $1.4M federal grant aiming to improve rural healthcare access. This initiative may address Oklahoma's high rural maternal healthcare disparities, with only 27% of rural hospitals offering labor and delivery services.

headline: Measles cases reach 4,080 for the year — the highest in decades
summary: Measles cases in the U.S. have reached a 35-year high, with over 4,000 cases and five deaths reported in Pennsylvania alone. Most cases are among unvaccinated individuals. Public health efforts include vaccination clinics and awareness campaigns in affected areas, while the federal government offers funding and addresses vaccine injury concerns.

headline: North Carolina records first reported flu-related death of the season
summary: North Carolina records its first flu-related death of the 2026-2027 season; health officials urge vaccination by October.

headline: Kansas Gov. Laura Kelly rallies Iowa educators for Sand’s campaign
summary: Kansas Gov. Laura Kelly endorsed Iowa's Democratic gubernatorial candidate Rob Sand, emphasizing Sand's bipartisan approach. She criticized Republican opponent Zach Lahn's residency and educational policies. No protests or civil unrest were mentioned.

headline: Measles hits the 100-case mark in Kentucky
summary: Kentucky has confirmed over 100 measles cases this year, with 102 occurring in unvaccinated individuals. Health officials urge Kentuckians to get the MMR vaccine to protect against measles, which is highly contagious and can lead to severe health complications.
